  "text": "The library's smallest table had developed a wobble that defeated three folded leaflets and a biography of Wellington.

“Perhaps it's the floor,” said Martin.

“Then we'll need a larger biography,” said Ruth.

She came every Tuesday to return a gardening book and borrow another, although Martin had never seen her garden.

“What are you growing this year?” he asked.

“Optimistic,” she said.

He wasn't sure whether this was a variety of potato.

On her next visit, Ruth brought a spirit level wrapped in a tea towel.

“My husband's,” she said. “He used to check everything. Shelves, picture frames, cakes.”

“Cakes?”

“He felt a slope gave someone an unfair advantage.”

They cleared the table. Ruth laid the level across it, then turned it the other way.

“Short leg,” she announced.

Martin fetched the library's toolbox, which contained a screwdriver, six drawing pins, and a key labelled UNKNOWN.

Ruth examined the key.

“Best keep that. You might find the door.”

She took a cork from her handbag and cut a thin disc with her penknife. Martin lifted the table while she fitted it beneath the offending leg.

The wobble stopped.

They stood back, quietly pleased.

“Will you want the level returned?” Martin asked.

“Eventually. I haven't baked anything competitive lately.”

He offered her first use of the repaired table.

Ruth sat down and opened her gardening book. Martin brought over a cup of tea, placing it carefully beside her.

“Nothing spilled,” he said.

“A promising start.”

The following Tuesday, she brought him a small pot of seedlings.

“Tomatoes,” she said, before he could ask. “The garden's full.”"
